closure of visceral and parietal peritoneums
finding: Closure of both visceral and parietal peritoneum during cesarean section was associated with increased postoperative pain, decreased urine output, and higher sympathetic activity (higher pulse rate and blood pressure).
mod_finding: Closure of both visceral and parietal peritoneum during cesarean section should be avoided as it is associated with increased postoperative pain and sympathetic overactivity.
